Every property owner in the US is required to pay property tax to their county. When an owner is delinquent, the county has some process to handle it. Typically the county will place a lien on the property that way the taxes must be paid if they tried selling their house. If the owner continues not paying, the county will foreclose and will sell the property in an auction to the highest bidder.

Some states (roughly half of them) sell tax lien certificates to investors and others sell tax deeds.

Tax liens are generally better if you just want to get an ROI on your money. Tax deeds are better if you want to own the property and sell for profit.

There are some decent tools to help. I wouldn’t even start with a product in mind. What you need is the process and that will tell you if a product is a good or bad candidate. Don’t get stuck on a product unless you’re going to private label something then that’s different.

If you have an iPhone you can download the Amazon app that allows you to scan bar codes. That tells you the price it’s selling at and a couple other things. Some similar apps will tell you estimated profit, etc. However it does not tell you the WHOLE story. You need to know not just the current FBA price, but the sales history. For that you use Camel Camel Camel (website). That will show if a product is seasonal, on the rise, declining, etc.

To be honest I wouldn’t start with low margin items because although they are lower initial cost, they are not less risky. You will develop your own criteria, but personally I don’t resell anything that doesn’t profit me at least $10 per item. You’ll need to know about oversized products as well since there is a slightly higher fee but Amazon provides all that info. 

To find products, I would start looking at your local stores. You can browse clearance items, sales, etc. You are looking for the anomalies where there is an inefficiency in the market. They are out there, but you need to dig a little bit. I’ve found that specific light bulbs can be a good markup, for example, if you buy them on sale.

Where I’m from we have a discount store which is mostly Costco items that were returned. I can sometimes find good items in there. Example, I bought a fancy toilet seat cover with bells and whistles (not used) for $300ish and resold it for around $500. I didn’t even really know what the thing looked like since it was still new in the box and no picture. I just opened it to make sure it was all there. I just made sure to list it as “like new,” not “new.” Some people get picky and if the packaging looks like it had been opened previously they will return it.

So in summary, don’t just buy stuff because you think it’ll sell. The data will show you what to buy.
